about: The gloss dictionary. Each code has a full word ('words', the default style) and a short word ('short', the compact style). Full words are lower case, a group then the action, with a third part for less common codes: run.* for moves and other things the machine does on that line (run.rapid, run.feed, run.pause, run.home), set.* for modes that stay in effect (set.inch, set.abs, set.fpm, set.sfm, set.smax), and a feature name for the rest (ccomp.left, tlen.on, cool.on, spindle.fwd, cycle.peck, call.macro). The same meaning has the same full word on every control, so a code that means something else on one control gets a different word there. Address letters keep an upper-case prefix before their value (SEQ10, TOOL1, INCX0.5). A code whose meaning differs between machine types has 'mill' and 'lathe' entries. Machine definition files can override any entry; an older file with a 'long' word still reads, using it as the full word. machineOverrides keys are a brand ('haas') or a brand and machine type ('okuma.mill'); the more specific key wins.
